players.product: power transformers and grid equipment buyer — US utility (largest HD Hyundai Electric customer)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO John Ketchum on federal hubs since the Q2 call: NextEra now has 16 GW of federal hub opportunities — 10 GW with the Japanese fund, with $3.3 billion of capital already in the door on those first 10 GW (the first two capital calls; 'it could be more as we get through the year'), plus the 6.5 GW Project Star with Korea and the U.S. Department of Commerce, funded $2.4 billion on the day of the conference. Adding the 4.6 GW at Paducah with the U.S. Department of Energy (half gas, half storage) brings the total to 20.5 GW and the gas build tally to 18 GW, versus 24 GW of installed gas at FPL today; behind that sits a pipeline of 40 data center hubs. NextEra puts no capital into the federal hub projects (owned by the federal government and Japan or Korea through a private special purpose vehicle); it earns development fees, milestone fees and two operating fees after COD (one fixed, one variable), a fee stream of roughly 50% of the adjusted EPS it would earn building the gas plant on its own balance sheet, with some fees at risk on milestones and operating requirements. CEO: counting 16 GW as 8 GW on that basis puts NextEra 'already at the high end' of the 4-8 GW of gas expected for 2032 in December, and adding the 2 GW of gas for Paducah takes it to 10 GW ('already chipping away at 2033'). The S-4 included one federal hub; there are now three. He named the Anderson project right outside of Dallas (5.2 gigawatts), where Comstock will provide the gas supply, and said 'I would expect that there could be more opportunities to follow' with the Departments of Commerce and Energy.
quarterly_data.figure: 16 GW of federal hubs (10 GW Japan, 6.5 GW Project Star); $3.3 billion capital received on the first 10 GW; $2.4 billion funded on Project Star; 20.5 GW incl. 4.6 GW Paducah; 18 GW gas tally; 40 data center hubs; fee stream roughly 50% of self-build adjusted EPS

quarterly_data.signal: CEO ('this is new news'): NextEra has all the rights to build the battery storage capacity that will serve the three federal hubs (16 gigawatts); this 6-11 gigawatt incremental battery storage build opportunity is not in its financial or development expectations and is upside to the forecast laid out for investors. CEO also expects battery storage to play a bigger role at data centers, as backup generation capability (a diesel substitute) and by moving from a capacity opportunity to a voltage regulation compliance market, citing voltage fluctuations attributed to some data centers: 'we're very, very focused on that as a huge business opportunity for us.' Every gas project NextEra builds also comes with a storage opportunity and a CFE element.
quarterly_data.figure: 6-11 gigawatt incremental battery storage opportunity at the federal hubs, not in financial expectations

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on equipment and rates: 'we bought our equipment out through 2030... We have our equipment bought, signed up, and contracted through 2030' — already physically and financially hedged. On renewables and storage NextEra match funds, with $46 billion of hedges in place, putting its interest rate sensitivity at $0.01-$0.03 in 2028; the federal hub gas build carries no rate exposure because NextEra commits no capital, and its milestone payments to equipment suppliers and EPC contractors are tied to the capital that flows in, so it is 'never overextended or over-committed to a supplier of equipment'. CEO: 'I don't see any downturn in the demand for the renewable or the storage opportunities'.
quarterly_data.figure: equipment bought and contracted through 2030; $46 billion of hedges; interest rate sensitivity $0.01-$0.03 in 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on the power market: the excess capacity on the system of 3 or 4 years ago is 'gone... That's been spoken for'; with the FERC show cause order and Independent System Operators asking that new load be paired with generation (he cited the FERC-approved Southwest Power Pool model, where generation must be 2 substations away), load and generation must work together early. Hyperscaler conversations at scale are never one-size-fits-all (e.g. starting at 1 gig of compute capacity and moving to 3 or 4 or 5), speed to power often starts with solar and storage with gas brought in behind it, and hyperscalers now show 'a real willingness to work together early on'. On demand: 'I just don't see that demand slowing down anytime soon'; the federal hubs exist because 'we're desperately short energy generation in this country to accommodate data center supply'.

CEO on progress since the Q2 call and in the first nine months: recontracted Point Beach ('a very attractive contract'); announced a 49% interest in a gas pipeline being built in Florida by Chesapeake; the linear infrastructure business (electric transmission and gas pipelines), targeted at a 20% CAGR, is at a 25% CAGR in the first nine months, with two major transmission projects brought forward; roughly 2 GW of PPAs recontracted against an 8 GW target through 2032, 'into a much higher price market'; and after the Symmetry acquisition NextEra is the third largest gas marketer and third largest power marketer in the U.S.
quarterly_data.figure: 49% interest in Chesapeake's Florida gas pipeline; linear infrastructure 25% CAGR vs 20% target; roughly 2 GW recontracted vs 8 GW target through 2032

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on the Dominion Energy combination: the combined company is expected to move from 110 gigawatts to roughly 240 gigawatts by 2032, as filed in the S-4. In Virginia, Amazon filed to give up the large load credits it was receiving and reallocate them to residential customers; NextEra topped that off with another $85 million commitment, taking residential credits from 2 years to 4 years, and committed to spend $1 billion a year in Virginia with suppliers doing business in the state. CEO noted Virginia has 20 GW of storage that has to be built under statutory mandate by 2044. 'Feeling really good about it.'
quarterly_data.figure: 110 GW to roughly 240 GW by 2032; $85 million added commitment (residential credits 2 to 4 years); $1 billion a year Virginia supplier spend

connects_to.relationship: power for Google data centers — collaboration to recommission NextEra's Duane Arnold nuclear plant (cited as the example of NextEra's channel of working directly with hyperscalers to power their data centers)

contracts.signal: CEO: the Duane Arnold recommissioning 'is going very well'; 'Google is the offtaker there on that facility. They will pay for 100% of the power generation.'
